content:
Hi all, I'm an independent researcher and this is my first post here. I've released a preprint, Operationistic Grasslands: A Framework for Radical-Remainder Quotients on ℕ, with a complete Lean 4 / Mathlib4 formalization on github.

It generalizes residue systems: instead of cutting ℕ into equal-width classes (ordinary modular arithmetic), the classes, the "chapters", are allowed to vary in width. The family I study comes from the radical remainder: how far a number sits above the largest perfect n-th power below it. Most of the results are about how equivalences between integers form and break across degrees, with classical modular arithmetic recovered as the flat special case.

Everything is machine-checked in Lean 4, except two intentionally documented open results.

:document: Paper/Preprint
:computer: Github Code

Feedback from number theorists and the Lean community especially welcome.
